title: Pretend you're my mom
author: Storytime
hook: Eight years ago, a teenage girl grabbed my arm at the mall and whispered, please pretend you're my mom. Last Saturday, I finally found out who she was.
story: Eight years ago, I was Christmas shopping at the mall. A girl, maybe fifteen, walked up, linked her arm in mine, and whispered, please pretend you're my mom. There's a man following me. I didn't think. I said loudly, there you are, sweetie, your dad's waiting in the car. I saw a man behind her stop, turn around, and leave. I walked her to mall security and waited until her real mom came. She hugged me so hard. I never got her name. Last Saturday was my daughter's college graduation. The student speaker walked up to the podium. She said, I want to tell you about the day a stranger saved my life. And she told my story. The mall. The man. The woman who said, your dad's waiting in the car. She said that man was arrested two weeks later. He had followed three other girls. She said, I studied criminal justice because of her. I don't know her name. I just hope she knows. My daughter turned to me, crying, and said, Mom, that was you, wasn't it? Should I go say hi?
caption: your dad's waiting in the car 🛍️ #storytime
sound: a gentle, emotional piano with a slow swell at very low volume
why: Stranger helping someone who is followed is trending, the mall line is a perfect callback, the graduation speech twist is deeply moving, and should I go say hi invites heartfelt comments.

title: My son asked Santa for a lawyer
author: Storytime
hook: My eight year old's Christmas list had only one thing on it. A lawyer.
story: Every year, my son Max writes a Christmas list for Santa. Usually it's Lego, a dinosaur, maybe a drone. This year, I opened his letter. It said, Dear Santa, I only want one thing. A lawyer. A real one. Please. I laughed, then I got worried. So I asked him why. He crossed his arms and said, because Lily stole my idea. Lily is his eleven year old sister. Two weeks ago, she won first place at the school science fair. Her project was a volcano that erupts glitter instead of lava. Max says it was his idea. He says he told her about it at breakfast in September. Lily says he's lying. They haven't spoken to each other in two weeks. Dinner has been very quiet. So I did what any reasonable parent would do. I checked the family tablet. And there it was. A drawing Max made in September. A volcano. Glitter. Labeled, my science fair idea, do not steal. With his signature. And a little stick figure of Lily, crying. Lily won a fifty dollar gift card and a trophy. Max wants half the gift card and an apology in front of the whole family on Christmas morning. Who's right?
caption: he wants a lawyer for Christmas 🌋 #storytime
sound: a playful courtroom drama sting with a silly twist at very low volume
why: Kids' Christmas wish lists are a seasonal favorite, the lawyer request is a hilarious hook, the signed drawing is a funny piece of evidence, and the who's right question pulls comments.

title: My boss gave me a zero dollar gift card
author: Storytime
hook: Every Christmas, my boss gives everyone a twenty five pound gift card. This year, mine had nothing on it.
story: I've worked at the same small accounting firm for six years. Every December, our boss, Mr. Hale, hands out envelopes. Each one has a twenty five pound gift card and a little handwritten note. This year, everyone opened theirs at the same time. My coworkers cheered. I went to the shop at lunch to use mine. The cashier scanned it, frowned, and said, sorry, this card has zero balance. I felt sick. I thought, this is it. I'm being let go. I didn't sleep that night. The next morning, I asked Mr. Hale about it, trying not to sound upset. He looked surprised, then laughed. He said, did you not read the note? I hadn't. I'd thrown it away with the envelope. I dug through the office bin. Found it. It said, your gift isn't on this card. Starting January, you're the new office manager. Twenty percent raise. Please don't tell anyone until I announce it Friday. Then he whispered, and buy yourself something nice, the card was just a decoy. Now my coworkers keep asking what I bought with my gift card. What do I tell them?
caption: always read the note 💌 #storytime
sound: a cheerful office Christmas jingle with a gentle twist at very low volume
why: Holiday work gift season is starting, the empty card makes viewers fear the worst, the hidden promotion note is a satisfying twist, and the what do I tell them question invites funny answers.
